# Barcelona Family Trip Snapshot

A 3-day Barcelona plan for 2 adults + 2 children, built around **short walking distances**, **metro access**, and a **family-friendly apartment stay**. The budget target of **EUR 1,800 excluding flights** is realistic if you choose a mid-range apartment, mix paid and free activities, and keep dinners simple except for one food-focused evening.

## 3-Day Barcelona Itinerary and Budget Plan

| Day | Focus | Area to Stay/Start | Walking Target | Main Cost Driver | Est. Day Cost |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| Day 1 | Museum + Gothic Quarter | Eixample or El Born near metro | 6–8 km | Museum tickets + tapas lunch | EUR 230–320 |
| Day 2 | Park + Beach | Barceloneta / Poblenou / near L4 metro | 5–7 km | Transport + casual meals | EUR 200–290 |
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/aa/Beach%2C_Barcelona_%28P1170715%29.jpg Alt=| Day 2 | Park + Beach | Barceloneta / Poblenou / near L4 metro | 5–7 km | Transport + casual meals | EUR 200–290 |, Barcelona, Spain
| Day 3 | Food-focused evening | Eixample / Sant Antoni | 4–6 km | Special dinner + market snacks | EUR 260–380 |

### Day 1: Museum Day in Eixample and the Old City
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

- Morning: Arrive, check in, and settle into an apartment near **Passeig de Gràcia**, **Urquinaona**, or **Diagonal** metro.
- Late morning: Visit **Museu Picasso** or **CosmoCaixa** if you want a more child-friendly science option.
- Afternoon: Easy walk through the **Gothic Quarter** and along **La Rambla**; keep the route compact and stop often.
- Dinner: Early casual dinner in **El Born** with shared plates and kid-friendly options.
- Booking suggestion: Reserve timed museum entry in advance, especially for spring travel.

### Day 2: Park and Beach Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg

- Morning: Head to **Parc de la Ciutadella** for playground time, open space, and a relaxed start.
- Midday: Continue to **Barceloneta Beach** or choose **Parc del Poblenou** if you want less sand and a calmer pace.
- Afternoon: Ice cream break and a short seaside stroll; avoid long crossings and keep it metro-based.
- Dinner: Simple neighborhood meal near your apartment, or picnic-style groceries if the kids are tired.
- Booking suggestion: No advance ticket needed for the park; beach day works best with a flexible schedule.

### Day 3: Food-Focused Evening in Sant Antoni or El Born
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

- Morning: Slow start with breakfast near the apartment and a short neighborhood walk.
- Afternoon: Visit **Mercat de Sant Antoni** or **Mercat de la Boqueria** for snacks, fruit, and a light lunch.
- Evening: Book a family-friendly tapas dinner with an early seating, ideally near **Sant Antoni** or **El Born**.
- Food idea: Share patatas bravas, croquetas, grilled seafood, tortilla, and dessert for the kids.
- Booking suggestion: Reserve dinner ahead, especially if you want a popular tapas spot with table service.

## Apartment and Cost Breakdown

| Category | Budget Range | Planning Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Lodging, 3 nights | EUR 720–1,050 | Apartment-style stay near a metro station; 1–2 bedroom layout preferred |
| Food | EUR 420–560 | Breakfast in apartment, lunch casual, one nicer dinner |
| Local transport | EUR 60–110 | Metro, airport transfer, occasional taxis if needed |
| Activities | EUR 180–280 | Museum tickets, optional guided entry, small extras |
| Buffer | EUR 90–180 | Snacks, ice cream, minor surprises |
| Total | **EUR 1,470–2,180** | Aim near **EUR 1,650–1,800** for comfort within budget |

## Best Stay Areas for This Family Trip

- **Eixample**: Best all-round choice for metro access, wider sidewalks, and apartment availability.
- **El Born**: Good for museums and central sightseeing, but a bit busier.
- **Poblenou**: Strong option for beach access and a calmer family feel.
- **Sant Antoni**: Great food area with practical metro connections and good value.
